newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Deutsche Bank expands Sydney operations.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank expands Sydney operations.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG group is to expand its Australian operations, creating 500 direct jobs and lifting its total work force to 1,700 by the year 2001, the New South Wales government said in a statement on Saturday.
New South Wales (NSW) Premier Bob Carr said Deutsche will also move its Australian dollar funds management and regional market operations to Sydney from London and Singapore.
Deutsche said in May after it won a tender for the NSW government's Axiom funds management business with a A$240 million bid that it would move some of its asset management business to Sydney.

"The group, which is the largest German organisation investing in Australia, proposes to use the purchase of Axiom to establish a world class asset manager in Sydney," managing director of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Australia, John Barnes, said in a statement.

Since Deutsche Bank acquired Sydney-based broking house Bain and Company in 1989, the group had grown in Australia from 600 staff to 1,200 and is expected to employ another 500 people by the year 2001.
